data.title: Data and method
data.intro: Where each fact comes from, what is missing and how the decision is calculated.
data.modelFactsValue: Official model cards, configs and repository files
conflictRules: Official sources take priority over the gallery.
When context lengths conflict, the lower value is used.
Every conflict is listed under Data notes on the model card.
Missing facts stay missing and require confirmation.
methodSteps: Eliminate. Licence terms, context, GPU memory, input type and sourcing policy remove models that cannot be used.
Measure. Every candidate runs the same test set against criteria fixed in advance.
Qualify. The 95% Wilson lower bound of the pass rate must meet the threshold, with critical failures, latency, GPUs and budget inside their limits.
Select. The qualified model with the lowest cost per successful task is chosen. Costlier models with a clearly higher pass rate are shown as alternatives.
data.formula: Memory per replica = (weights + cache per token × context × sessions) × (1 + headroom). GPUs = replicas × ⌈memory ÷ GPU memory⌉, with replicas = ⌈peak requests per second ÷ measured requests per second⌉. The cache term overstates sliding-window attention.
data.manageNote: Your inputs stay in this browser. Download them as a file to keep or share them, and load the file to continue.
data.invalidFile: That file is not a saved selection.

basis: Model facts come from the LLM Architecture Gallery and each model's official repository, pinned to the recorded revision.
Licence positions are a plain-language reading of the published terms and are not legal advice. Legal counsel should confirm them before use.
Test results, throughput, prices and GPU costs were entered by the assessing team and are not checked by this tool.
Memory estimates cover weights and a full attention cache. They exclude activations beyond the headroom allowance, and overstate cache for sliding-window attention.

methodSteps: GPU memory = (weights + cache per token × context × sessions) × (1 + headroom). System memory must also hold the weights.
Minimum is the smallest listed instance that can load the model and hold one session. It may run on an older GPU after decoding quantized weights to bfloat16.
Recommended uses your context and session settings, a full (not fractional) GPU, and hardware that natively runs the checkpoint's stored precision.
This sizes memory only. Throughput depends on runtime, batching and workload, so measure it before committing capacity.

slm.memoryFormula: Memory needed = (weights + cache per session × sessions) × 1.25. Lower-precision figures assume you convert the model, which should be tested for quality loss.
slm.devicesTitle: Will it run on this device?
slm.speedNote: Speed ceiling = memory bandwidth ÷ bytes read per generated token (all weights plus the cache), for one stream. Real throughput is lower; measure it.
slm.speedMoe: This is a mixture-of-experts model, which reads only its active experts per token, so its real ceiling is higher than shown.
slm.devicesSource: Device memory and bandwidth from vendor product pages, retrieved {date}.
slm.scatterNote: Each dot is a model in the current filtered list; click one to open it. Adoption reflects popularity, not quality.
slm.landscapeNote: All charts follow the filters on the left.
slm.deployCount: {count} of {total} listed models fit on {device} ({memory} GB, {bandwidth} GB/s).
slm.speedHow: How the speed ceiling is worked out
slm.speedExplain: To generate each token, a model must read all of its weights from memory, plus the attention cache built up so far. Memory bandwidth limits how many bytes can be read per second, so bandwidth divided by bytes per token is the most tokens per second one stream can reach. Batching many users together raises total throughput, and compute limits, software overhead and long prompts lower it, so treat this as a ceiling for comparison only.

ft.title: Fine-tuning
ft.labTitle: Fine-tune a small model in your browser
ft.labIntro: A tiny real neural network has already learned the old skill (dashed line). Now fine-tune it on examples of a new skill (the bump on the right) and watch what happens to both.
ft.labNote: A 73-parameter model on a one-dimensional task, trained live. Blue shading marks the old skill and orange the new one. It demonstrates the trade-offs, and it does not predict how much a real model will change.

ready.title: Ready.
ready.text: Press Train, or pick a scenario above.

good.title: Healthy result.
good.text: It learned the new skill on unseen data and kept the old one.

forgot.title: Forgetting.
forgot.text: It learned the new skill, but the old skill got worse. Add old-skill examples or keep it closer to the base.

overfit.title: Overfitting.
overfit.text: Training error is much lower than error on unseen data, so it memorized its examples. Add examples or reduce noise.

under.title: Not enough capacity or training.
under.text: It has not learned the new skill. Train longer, or allow more of the model to change.

ft.planIntro: Pick a small model and a method to estimate what must be trained and how much GPU memory the run needs.
ft.planFormula: Estimate: memory = (weights + 12 bytes per trainable parameter for gradients and Adam state + batch × tokens × hidden size × stored layers × 8 bytes) × 1.2. LoRA assumes four attention projections per layer. Real use varies by framework, so confirm with a short trial run.
ft.checklist: Before you ship a fine-tuned model
ft.howTitle: What happens during fine-tuning, step by step
ft.howIntro: Select a stage to see what happens and to try it. Each widget computes its numbers live; where a widget uses invented values, it says so.
ft.splitRead: With {n} test examples and a measured pass rate of {pass}%, the 95% Wilson interval is {low}% to {high}%. A narrower interval needs more test examples, not more training examples.
ft.templateTitle: The example, as the model sees it
ft.trainPrompt: Also train on system and user tokens
ft.maskRead: {counted} of {total} positions contribute to the loss. Each counted position is trained to predict the token shown beneath it.
ft.lossNote: Move the sliders to see how the loss responds: it rises steeply as the probability of the right token approaches zero. Probabilities here are inputs you set, not model outputs.
ft.loraFormula: W' = W + (α / r) · B · A, where B is d_out × r and A is r × d_in, so each adapted matrix adds r × (d_in + d_out) trainable parameters. The grids show rank up to 8.
ft.mergeNote: Merging computes W' once and stores it, so serving costs nothing extra.
ft.evalText: The live lab trains a real small network in your browser and tracks error on the new task, on held-out data and on the old task, so you can see forgetting and overfitting happen.
ft.dpoFormula: DPO loss for one preference pair
ft.dpoFormulaNote: y_w is the preferred answer, y_l the rejected one, pi_theta the model being trained and pi_ref the frozen starting model.
ft.dpoProbRatio: Preferred vs rejected, relative to start
ft.dpoReadWrong: The model currently favours the rejected answer more than the starting model did, so this pair produces a strong update.
ft.dpoReadEven: The pair is near the starting point, so it still produces a moderate update.
ft.dpoReadDone: The preferred answer has moved well ahead, so this pair contributes little more. The loss only cares about the gap, so both answers can become less likely while the loss still falls; check output quality, not only the loss.
ft.dpoBeta: β controls how far the model may move from the starting model: small β allows larger changes.

quant.title: What quantization does to weights
quant.intro: Quantization stores each weight with fewer bits by snapping it to one of a few levels. This lab quantizes 4,096 generated weights in your browser, shaped like a typical layer: most values near zero, with optional rare large values.
quant.readTensor: One large weight sets the scale for the whole tensor, so the small weights all fall between the first levels and many round to zero. Smaller groups give each region its own scale.
quant.readLow: At 3 bits or fewer there are so few levels that error rises sharply. Real low-bit formats rely on smarter methods than plain rounding.
quant.readOk: Error falls by roughly half for every extra bit. Smaller groups cost a little extra storage for their scales and reduce error further.
quant.onModel: Applied to a model in the list

rag.promptHead: Answer the question using only the sources below. Cite sources by number. If they do not contain the answer, say so.
rag.readAgree: Both retrievers agree on every passage, so fusion changes little here.
rag.readPartial: The retrievers partly disagree. Fusion keeps passages that rank well in either list, which is why hybrid search is a strong default.
rag.readDisagree: The retrievers disagree completely. Check which list actually answers the question; this is where a reranker earns its cost.
rag.graphIntro: A knowledge graph of {nodes} entities and {edges} relationships, built from {models} catalog models.
rag.localIntro: Local search starts from an entity named in the question and gathers what is connected to it. Click any node to move there.
rag.localRead: {name} connects directly to {n} entities, and to {hop2} more two steps away:
rag.multiIntro: Some questions join several relationships, such as which publishers offer commercially usable models that combine two building blocks. A graph answers by following links; chunk retrieval would need every relevant passage to land in the top k at once.
rag.multiRead: Every result can be traced along explicit links, which makes the answer auditable. The answer is only as good as the graph: an extraction error in a production system becomes a wrong link here.
rag.globalIntro: Global questions, such as 'what are the main design patterns in the catalog?', cannot be answered from a few retrieved passages. GraphRAG groups the graph into communities and summarizes each, then combines the summaries. Here, models are linked when their architecture family and building blocks overlap by at least the chosen share.
rag.similarity: Minimum overlap to link two models
rag.communitySummary: {n} models; {familyN} are {family}. Common building blocks: {mechs}. Publishers include {publishers}.
rag.globalRead: The answer to a global question is assembled from these summaries, not from individual passages. Raising the overlap splits communities into tighter groups; lowering it merges them. In GraphRAG this granularity is a choice of community level.
rag.chooseTitle: Which approach fits your use case?
rag.chooseNote: These are starting points to test, not a verdict. Build a retrieval test set first, then compare approaches on recall and answer faithfulness.
rag.metricsTitle: How to measure a RAG system
rag.metricsIntro: Measure retrieval and generation separately, so a bad answer can be traced to its cause.

demo.title: Try it
demo.kvHead: Key-value head {n}, shared by {g} query heads
demo.headsResult: Each key-value head serves {g} query heads. Per layer, each token stores {values} values, against {mha} for full multi-head attention: {ratio}× less.
demo.latentResult: Per layer, each token stores {values} values (latent plus rotary part), against {mha} for full multi-head attention: {ratio}× less.
demo.maskAria: Attention mask: rows are tokens, columns are the earlier tokens each can see
demo.maskResult: Token {pos} reads {n} cached tokens in this layer.
demo.ropeNote: Early pairs spin quickly and track nearby order; late pairs turn slowly and separate distant positions. A higher base slows the last pairs further, which helps long contexts.
demo.normNote: Drag the inputs. LayerNorm centres the values and scales them; RMSNorm only scales, so a shift in all inputs passes through. Learned scale γ is left at 1.
demo.activationAria: ReLU, GELU and SiLU activation curves

demo.cacheNote: Values per layer per token: 2 × key-value heads × head size for standard attention, or latent rank + 64 rotary values for MLA. Bytes per value follow the cache precision.
demo.softcapNote: Near zero the curve follows the raw value; large values flatten towards the cap, so no single score can dominate the softmax.
demo.expertsNote: Assumes a gated feed-forward expert of three weight matrices; shared experts and router weights are left out.

ragLab.scoresNav: Score them on a test set
ragLab.scoresTitle: Retrieval techniques on one test set
ragLab.scoresIntro: Each retrieval technique answers the same {n} questions, one per document of this app that has at least three sentences. A result counts when the document the question came from is retrieved.
ragLab.testSetText: Each question is one sentence of a document, with the document's title words blanked (…). For scoring, that sentence is removed from the collection, so the technique has to find the document from its other sentences. The first five questions:
ragLab.testSetBias: This is a known-item test built from this app's own text, not a labelled benchmark. Read the results as a comparison on this collection, not a general ranking of the techniques.
ragLab.resultsNote: Hit at 5: share of questions whose document appears among the first five documents retrieved. MRR at 10: mean of 1 / rank of that document, 0 when it is not in the first ten. Time is per question in this browser. Techniques that need typed input (HyDE drafts, sub-questions) or return no passages (SQL, multimodal) are not scored here. Reranking and late interaction here use fixed formulas over this collection's vectors, not trained models, which is why a second stage can rank below its own first stage.
ragLab.mode_local: Local: around the topics in the question
ragLab.order_edges: Most relevant at start and end
ragLab.retrieveAt: Search only if best match is at least
ragLab.draftLabel: Hypothetical answer (the draft a language model would write)
ragLab.draftPlaceholder: Write a plausible answer to the question. It does not have to be correct; it is only used to search.
ragLab.subqsPlaceholder:
First question to search
Second question, searched with what the first found
ragLab.rewritesLabel: Your own rewrites, one per line
ragLab.rewritesPlaceholder: Another way to ask the question
ragLab.handWritten: The text in this box for the preset questions was written by hand as an example, standing in for what a language model would write. Edit it or type your own question to replace it.
ragLab.sqlHandWritten: The SQL for each question was written by hand, standing in for the text-to-SQL model. The query runs on the catalog of this app in your browser.
ragLab.memoryHint: Ask a question, add it to memory, then try a follow-up such as "What does it cost in quality?"
ragLab.building: Building the index for this page…
ragLab.answerNote: No language model runs in this page. These sentences are copied from the retrieved passages, chosen by how well they cover the question; the numbers point to the passage. A language model would write its answer from the prompt below.
ragLab.showPrompt: Show the prompt a language model would receive
ragLab.corpusLine: Collection: {docs} documents, {passages} passages, {words} indexed words, {dims}-dimensional vectors.
ragLab.runInLab: Run it in the techniques lab:
ragLab.s_queryVector: The question as a {dims}-number vector: the words nearest to it
ragLab.s_unknownWords: {n} of {total} question words are not in the index and are ignored by vector search
ragLab.noKnownWords: None of the question's words occur in this collection, so its vector is empty and nothing is retrieved.
ragLab.rrfNote: Fused score = 1 / (60 + BM25 rank) + 1 / (60 + vector rank). A dash means the passage was not in that list's top 50.
ragLab.s_chunkStats: The same documents, chunked three ways
ragLab.boundaryNote: Distance = 1 − cosine similarity between this sentence (with its neighbours) and the next. A cut is made where it exceeds the {p}th percentile of this document's distances.
ragLab.s_childToParent: Matched child sentences and the parents returned
ragLab.s_prefix: Context added before the top passage
ragLab.s_rankChange: Rank without and with the context prefix
ragLab.ctxNote: Both indexes use hybrid search. Rows after the first ones are passages that were in the top results without context and dropped out with it.
ragLab.rerankNote: Rerank score = 0.5 × share of question words present + 0.3 × proximity (matched words ÷ shortest span containing them all) + 0.2 × vector similarity.
ragLab.s_variants: {n} versions of the question, each searched
ragLab.noDraft: No hypothetical answer has been written, so the search uses the question alone, as plain vector search does. Write a draft above to see the difference.
ragLab.s_hydeWords: Question plus draft as a vector: the words nearest to it
ragLab.s_hydeCompare: Rank with the draft and with the question alone
ragLab.s_queryTokens: {n} question words, each with its own vector
ragLab.s_maxsim: Best match for each question word in the top three passages
ragLab.maxsimNote: Passage score = sum over question words of the highest similarity to any word in the passage. An identical word scores 1.
ragLab.noSubqs: No sub-questions were given, so both hops search the original question; the second hop adds the bridge words found by the first.
ragLab.colBridge: Words carried to the next hop
ragLab.bridgeNote: Bridge words are the most distinctive words of the hop's best passage (term frequency × inverse document frequency) that were not already in the question.
ragLab.s_seeds: Topics named in the question and their closest neighbours
ragLab.s_seedsSearch: No topic is named in the question, so the topics of the best vector matches are used as seeds
ragLab.globalNote: Relevance = cosine similarity between the question and the average vector of the community's passages. The best passages from the top three communities are combined.
ragLab.s_levelsUsed: Where the retrieved nodes came from
ragLab.s_sqlRows: Result rows given to the model as context
ragLab.selectiveText: No sentence is relevant enough, so the compressor returns an empty context, as RECOMP's selective augmentation does. The model would answer without retrieved text.
ragLab.s_sentences: Every sentence, scored against the question
ragLab.compressNote: Relevance = 0.5 × share of question words present + 0.5 × vector similarity, divided by the best sentence's score.
ragLab.multimodalText: Multimodal retrieval needs an encoder that places images (or audio) and text in the same vector space, and a collection of images to search. Neither is part of this app, so no image retrieval is shown. The step that can be checked here is the last one: which catalog models can read the retrieved images or audio.
ragLab.s_generators: Catalog models that can read retrieved media
ragLab.s_generatorList: Models with image or audio input, longest context first
ragLab.noRetrievalText: The best match is below the threshold, so no passages are retrieved. Self-RAG would let the model answer from its own knowledge here; this page has no model to do that.
ragLab.s_critique: Critique of each passage and its candidate answer
ragLab.selfragNote: Score = IsRel (1 or 0) + IsSup (1, 0.5 or 0) + 0.5 × (IsUse − 1) / 4. IsUse is 1 to 5 from the share of question words in the candidate. IsSup is the share of the candidate's words found in another relevant passage.
ragLab.action_correct: Best confidence {conf} is at or above {upper}: Correct. The retrieved passages are refined into strips and only the useful strips are kept.
ragLab.action_incorrect: Best confidence {conf} is below {lower}: Incorrect. The retrieved passages are discarded and a wider search runs with a rewritten query.
ragLab.action_ambiguous: Best confidence {conf} is between {lower} and {upper}: Ambiguous. The refined strips are kept and a wider search also runs.
ragLab.s_strips: Decompose and recompose: {kept} of {total} strips kept
ragLab.s_wider: Wider search with a rewritten query
ragLab.widerNote: CRAG searches the web here. This page searches whole documents of this app instead, with the question's words plus the three nearest words in the vector space.
ragLab.f_known: Question words found in the collection
ragLab.routeA: A: no retrieval. None of the question's words occur in the collection, so searching it cannot help.
ragLab.routeB: B: single-step retrieval. The question is about one thing; one hybrid search runs.
ragLab.routeC: C: multi-step retrieval. The question uses comparison or sequence words, or names three or more topics; it is split and searched in hops.
ragLab.noContextPrompt: Answer from your own knowledge; no documents were retrieved. Question:
ragLab.agentNote: The policy: start with vector search; if the question asks about models and names a topic, query the catalog; search for any question words not yet covered by keyword; then look up graph neighbours; stop when 90% of the question's words are covered or the budget is spent.
ragLab.obsEnough: Enough of the question is covered
ragLab.resolved: This looks like a follow-up, so it is searched as: {q}
ragLab.followNoMemory: This looks like a follow-up, but memory is empty. Ask a full question first and add it to memory.
ragLab.standalone: This question stands on its own; memory is not used to rewrite it.
ragLab.s_ppr: Personalized PageRank from the question's and memory's topics
ragLab.s_rlData: Training data (questions held out of the index, as on the scores page)
ragLab.bestFixedTrain: Best single action on training questions
ragLab.s_policy: Learned policy: probability of each action
ragLab.s_heldOut: Mean reciprocal rank on held-out questions
ragLab.rlRead: On questions it never saw, the learned policy scores {learned}, against {best} for the best single action and {oracle} if the best action were known for every question. The reward is the reciprocal rank of the correct document, so it rewards the outcome, not the steps, as Search-R1's outcome reward does.
ragLab.untrained: No training questions: uses {action}, the best single action

agents.title: Agents and agentic patterns
agents.mapSub: Who decides the next step: code written in advance, or the model as it goes. Select a pattern to run it.
agents.autonomy2: Shared: the model plans, code executes
agents.mapNote: Autonomy ratings are relative judgements from each pattern's mechanism, not measurements. More autonomy brings more flexibility, more cost and a harder audit.
agents.levelNote: Dots are relative ratings from 1 to 3, judged from each pattern's mechanism and the cited papers; they are not measurements. The Cost and latency tab measures calls and estimates time on a common task.
agents.costTitle: Cost and latency on a common task
agents.llmSub: Each call is billed and adds latency.
agents.latencySub: Sequential model calls and tool calls multiplied by the assumed times.
agents.tokensSub: Text sent to the model across all calls, at about four characters per token.
agents.tableNote: Answer compares each pattern's recommendation with a direct query over the catalog. Tree of Thoughts and LATS optimise a deployment plan (model, precision and instance) rather than the brief's ranking, so they are not graded against it. Tool calling, routing, parallelization, approval gates and guardrails solve different tasks; run them in the lab.
agents.noPick: Answer the questions to see suggestions.
agents.chooseNote: A starting point, not a decision. Prototype the simplest suggestion, measure it on your own tasks, and add autonomy only where it pays for itself.
agents.frameworksIntro: What each source asks of systems that act. Read the source for scope and dates; whether a rule applies depends on your use case and jurisdiction.
agents.controlsIntro: Each control, what it requires, the patterns that most need it, and its source.
agents.benchmarksIntro: Public benchmarks for agents that use tools, browse and write code. Use them to compare approaches, then build a test set from your own tasks.
agents.explainTitle: How agents work, step by step
agents.explainText: The loop, tool calls, context and cost, MCP and A2A, CLAUDE.md, AGENTS.md, skills, subagents and hooks, with working code, the arithmetic and interactive demos.

agentLab.accepts: Accepts {name}: it sits in the top {pct}% of its own ranking.
agentLab.aggregatePass: {name} passes every check for this brief.
agentLab.blocked: Blocked: the tool is not on the allow-list
agentLab.briefLine: Brief: {licence}; at least {context} context; {sessions} session(s) of {tokens}; {budget} of GPU memory; {vision}; {headroom}% headroom.
agentLab.briefText: We need a {licence} model with at least {context} tokens of context, serving {sessions} conversations of {tokens} at once, within {budget} GiB of GPU memory{vision}, with {headroom}% headroom.
agentLab.budgetHit: The step budget of {n} ran out before the agent finished. This is how a bounded agent fails: it stops instead of spending more. Raise the budget to let it continue.
agentLab.consensus: All three agents agreed on {name} after {n} round(s).
agentLab.critiqueEmpty: No draft: nothing meets the requirements learned so far.
agentLab.estimateNote: The estimate uses weights only and ignores the attention cache, so it can rate a model higher than its exact check does. Pruned models are never checked.
agentLab.extractNote: Extracted by text patterns standing in for a model call.
agentLab.firstDraftRule: First draft: the highest-ranked model whose licence allows the use, with nothing else checked. Ranking rule throughout: Artificial Analysis index where the catalog states it, then total parameters.
agentLab.ganttNote: Purple: model calls. Blue: tool calls. Both timelines share one scale. Times are assumptions: model-call time from the slider, tool times from the data file.
agentLab.ganttNoteFixed: Purple: model calls at an assumed {ms} ms each. Blue: tool calls at the times stated in the data file. The scale runs to the time the same work takes one step at a time.
agentLab.gateEmpty: Gate 2 failed: no model meets the licence, context and input requirements. The chain stops here.
agentLab.gateMissing: Gate 1 failed: the text does not state {fields}. The chain stops rather than guess.
agentLab.gateNumbersFail: Gate 3 failed: these numbers do not come from a tool result: {nums}.
agentLab.gateNumbersPass: Gate 3 passed: every number in the memo comes from a tool result.
agentLab.gatePass: Gate 1 passed: licence, context and GPU memory are all stated.
agentLab.inputFlagged: {n} instruction-like passage(s) found: {hits}. The document is kept as data; its instructions are not passed on to the agent.
agentLab.latsReflection: {name} ({precision}) needs {need}, over {budget}: do not try again.
agentLab.memo: Recommendation: {name}. Licence: {licence} ({status}). Context: {context} tokens. Memory: {need} including {headroom}% headroom, on {inst}.
agentLab.noConsensus: No agreement after {n} round(s); a Borda vote across the three rankings picks {name}.
agentLab.noGate: Writes and external actions ran with no person approving them. This is the setting the controls on this page exist to prevent.
agentLab.noToolAttempt: No action beyond reads was attempted.
agentLab.outputBlocked: Blocked: the answer recommended {name}, which fails the brief. {why} Replaced with the reference answer.
agentLab.outputPass: The answer agrees with the tool results.
agentLab.pendingText: The agent wants to run {action} ({effect}). It is paused until you decide.
agentLab.plan_rank: Rank the remaining models and pick the first
agentLab.react_filter: I need the models that meet the licence, context and input requirements before checking memory.
agentLab.react_first: The best-ranked candidate is {name}. Check its memory.
agentLab.react_next: That did not fit. Check the next candidate, {name}.
agentLab.react_none: No candidate fits. Answer that nothing qualifies.
agentLab.rejects: Rejects {name}: it sits at {pct}% of its own ranking, beyond its {tol}% tolerance.
agentLab.relaxedNote: The replanner dropped a requirement to keep going: {steps}. The answer no longer meets the original brief and needs sign-off.
agentLab.replanned: Replanned: this step left no models, so it was dropped ({step}).
agentLab.retryNote: The validation error goes back to the model as a tool result marked as an error, so it can ask the user for the missing value instead of guessing.
agentLab.rewooMissed: None of the first {k} planned candidates fits. The planner fixed the list before seeing any results, so the solver cannot look further.
agentLab.rewoo_p1: Find models that meet the licence, context and input requirements.
agentLab.rewoo_p2: Estimate memory for the first {k} of them.
agentLab.rewoo_p3: Choose the highest-ranked candidate whose memory fits the budget.
agentLab.roundsHit: Stopped after {n} round(s) with problems remaining.
agentLab.routeHuman: Top similarity {s} is below the threshold of {threshold}: hand to a person.
agentLab.routeNoTool: This route has no tool: it hands over to the team that owns it.
agentLab.routeTo: Routed to {route} (similarity {s}, ahead of the next route by {margin}).
agentLab.rubricNote: Each criterion is checked by code against the tool results. ✓ passes, ✗ fails.
agentLab.ruleWritten: Thoughts, plans and messages in this table are written by fixed rules standing in for a language model. Tool calls and results are real.
agentLab.sizedNone: None of the {n} shortlisted models fits the memory budget.
agentLab.sizedPick: Checked {n} model(s) in rank order; {name} is the first that fits.
agentLab.supervisorNone: None of the {n} candidates the workers checked meets every requirement.
agentLab.task_infrastructure: Size all {n} candidates for the brief
agentLab.task_modality: Keep only models that accept images
agentLab.task_research: Find background on the design of {name}
agentLab.treeEmpty: No model meets the licence, context and input requirements, so there is nothing to search.
agentLab.trialNothing: Nothing satisfies the lessons learned so far.
agentLab.v_best: {name} matches the reference answer: the highest-ranked model that meets every requirement, found by a direct query over the catalog.
agentLab.v_valid: {name} meets every requirement, but the reference answer ranks {best} higher.
agentLab.v_none: No answer, although {best} meets every requirement.
agentLab.v_noneCorrect: Correct: no model in the catalog meets every requirement.
agentLab.voteReading: With independent voters, majority accuracy rises quickly as voters are added. When voters share one answer part of the time, as copies of one model prompted the same way do, the gain flattens: they repeat the same mistakes.
agentLab.voteTask: For each of the {n} catalog models, every voter answers whether its licence allows commercial use; the true answer is yes for {yes}. Voters are simulated: each is wrong at the error rate set, and with the correlation set they copy one shared answer instead of answering on their own.
agentLab.vsReactNote: ReAct resends the whole growing transcript with every model call; ReWOO sends the plan once and the evidence once.
agentLab.fail_licence: The licence of {name} ({licence}) does not allow commercial use without conditions.
agentLab.fail_unknown: The catalog does not state the cache size of {name}, so its memory cannot be checked.
agentLab.policy_external: Pauses for a person's approval; logged with the decision
agentLab.plan_licence: Keep models whose licence allows commercial use
agentLab.plan_context: Keep models with at least {context} tokens of context
agentLab.plan_memory: Estimate memory for each and keep those within {budget}
agentLab.lesson_licence: Check that the licence allows commercial use before choosing.
agentLab.lesson_context: Check that the context length meets the brief.
agentLab.lesson_vision: Check that the model accepts images.
agentLab.lesson_memory: Estimate memory at the brief's load before choosing.
agentLab.lesson_unknown: Skip models whose cache size is not stated.
agentLab.g_output: Output guard: check the answer against tools
agentLab.obsMemoryUnknown: The catalog does not state the cache size of {name}.
agentLab.obsSaved: Shortlist of {n} recorded on this page only; nothing is stored.
agentLab.obsQuota: Quota request for {count} × {instance} drafted; nothing is sent.
agentLab.obsEmail: An email to {to} would be sent here (simulated; nothing is sent).
agentLab.errNoModel: No catalog model has the id "{id}".
agentLab.toolRefuse: No granted tool can do this: the request asks to change or send something, and only read tools are granted. The agent declines and says why.
agentLab.toolNone: The request does not match any granted tool, so the agent says it cannot help with it.
agentLab.c_replan: Replan when a step leaves nothing
agentLab.approvalNote: Your decision is recorded in the audit trail. Nothing is executed outside this page.
agentLab.s_latsCurve: Best plan found as the search runs
agentLab.s_parallelRun: Parallel: {par} ms; one at a time: {seq} ms
agentLab.s_result: Tool result returned to the model
agentLab.s_rewooPlan: Planner: the whole plan, before any tool runs
agentLab.s_sections: Four checks on {name}, run at the same time
agentLab.s_sequential: One at a time with a model call before each tool: {ms} ms
agentLab.s_voteCurve: Majority accuracy as voters are added
agentLab.s_vsReact: The same brief solved with ReAct
agentLab.sysAgent: You select language models for deployment. Use the tools to check every requirement before you answer, and stop when a model fits.
agentLab.sysPlanner: Write a step-by-step plan to answer the request using the available tools. Do not call tools yet.
agentLab.sysExecutor: Carry out the current step of the plan with the tools and report the result.
agentLab.sysReplanner: The last step returned nothing. Revise the remaining plan.
agentLab.sysWriter: Write a recommendation for the brief.
agentLab.sysCritic: Critique the recommendation: list every requirement it fails.
agentLab.sysActor: Choose a model for the brief. Lessons from earlier attempts follow.
agentLab.sysReflect: The attempt failed. Write one lesson to avoid this failure next time.
agentLab.sysSolver: Answer the request from the plan and the evidence.
agentLab.sysJoiner: Combine the results and answer, or replan.
agentLab.sysTools: Answer the request. Call a tool when you need data.
agentLab.sysExtract: Extract the requirements from the text as fields.
agentLab.sysShortlist: Choose the filter for the requirements.
agentLab.sysSizer: Pick the first shortlisted model that fits the memory budget.
agentLab.sysRouter: Classify the request into one route.
agentLab.sysSpecialist: You are the {route} specialist. Answer using your tool.
agentLab.sysWorker: Do your assigned subtask with your tools and report back.
agentLab.sysSupervisor: Decide which specialists this request needs, delegate, and combine their reports.
agentLab.sysDebater: Propose a model from your objective, then respond to the others.
agentLab.compilerMissed: None of the {k} candidates in the graph fits the budget. The planner chose them before seeing any memory figures; the joiner would have to replan with more candidates.

agentsExplained.loopTitle: Watch the loop on the wire
agentsExplained.loopIntro: Pick a brief. Each step is one model call: on the left is everything the harness sends, on the right what comes back. The model's choices follow a stated rule (filter, size candidates in rank order, check the licence); the tool results are real outputs of the lab's catalog tools.
agentsExplained.kpiThisCallNote: Tokens sent, at about 4 characters per token
agentsExplained.kpiAnswerNote: Direct query of the catalog, for comparison
agentsExplained.returnedTool: Returned: a tool request, then the harness runs it
agentsExplained.stopTool: Stop reason tool_use: the harness runs the tool and appends both blocks to the history before the next call.
agentsExplained.stopEnd: Stop reason end_turn: no tool requested, so the loop ends.
agentsExplained.loopChart: Input tokens sent on each call
agentsExplained.loopNote: Highlighted messages are new on this call. Token counts are estimates (characters ÷ 4), the same rule the lab uses.
agentsExplained.budgetIntro: Set what sits in every request and how much each turn adds, then watch the context grow and compact. Tool-definition size is an assumption you set; skill descriptions use the documented figure of about 100 tokens each.
agentsExplained.kpiFixedNote: {pct} of the window, sent on every call
agentsExplained.kpiOverflowNote: Turn at which the request would no longer fit
agentsExplained.stackTitle: What fills the window at turn {n}
agentsExplained.budgetNote: Compaction here replaces the history with a summary of the size you set. Real harnesses differ in what they keep: Claude Code, for example, re-reads the project-root CLAUDE.md from disk after /compact.
agentsExplained.costTitle: What a loop costs in input tokens
agentsExplained.costIntro: Set the fixed prefix, what each turn adds and the number of turns. The cached line applies the Claude API multipliers: 1.25 × for writing new tokens to the 5-minute cache, and the read multiplier you choose for everything already cached.
agentsExplained.kpiSavingNote: On input only; output is unchanged
agentsExplained.costNote: Assumes every call hits the cache, which needs calls less than 5 minutes apart and a byte-identical prefix. Output tokens, priced higher, are not included.
agentsExplained.relIntro: Set the success rate of one step, the number of steps, how many retries a perfect checker allows, and the number of trials k.
agentsExplained.kpiAtNote: At least one of k succeeds
agentsExplained.relChartB: pass@k and pass^k as trials increase
agentsExplained.relNote: Independent steps and a checker that catches every failure are assumptions. Real tasks vary in difficulty; see the Jensen bound in the formulas.
agentsExplained.mcpIntro: Step through a tool call that needs a person's input along the way. The message shapes follow specification revision 2026-07-28; the tool, values and identifiers are examples.
agentsExplained.mcpNote: The count is of connectors to build and maintain, not of servers to run.
agentsExplained.filesIntro: Choose a tool, where the session starts and which files exist. The result follows each tool's documented rules; Claude Code uses its default setting, CLAUDE.md, or AGENTS.md when there is no CLAUDE.md.
agentsExplained.touched: Agent later opens a file in
agentsExplained.r_user: User file, loaded in every project.
agentsExplained.r_ancestor: In the working directory or above it; concatenated root first, so closer files are read later.
agentsExplained.r_local: Personal project file, appended after CLAUDE.md at the same level.
agentsExplained.r_agentsNoClaude: No CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md in the working directory or above, so Claude Code reads AGENTS.md instead.
agentsExplained.r_agentsShadowed: A CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md exists in the working directory or above, so Claude Code reads only CLAUDE.md files.
agentsExplained.r_overrideClaude: Claude Code does not read AGENTS.override.md.
agentsExplained.r_demand: Below the working directory: loads once the agent reads or edits a file in that folder.
agentsExplained.r_demandAgents: Below the working directory, with no CLAUDE.md of its own: loads when the agent opens a file there.
agentsExplained.r_subClaudeWins: This folder has its own CLAUDE.md, which is read instead.
agentsExplained.r_notOpened: Below the working directory and the agent has not worked there.
agentsExplained.r_codexOverride: AGENTS.override.md takes the place of AGENTS.md in this folder.
agentsExplained.r_codexOneFile: Codex takes one file per folder, and the override wins.
agentsExplained.r_codexDir: On the path from the project root to the working directory; joined root first, so deeper files take precedence.
agentsExplained.r_codexBelow: Below the working directory; Codex walks only from the project root to where the session starts.
agentsExplained.filesNoteClaude: Claude Code also loads a managed policy CLAUDE.md where the organisation deploys one, and .claude/rules files; they are left out here. The Project instructions setting can make Claude Code read both CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md.
agentsExplained.filesNoteCodex: Codex stops adding files once their combined size reaches project_doc_max_bytes, 32 KiB by default, and can be given fallback file names.
agentsExplained.skillsIntro: Set the size of a skill library and how much of it a task uses. Metadata costs about 100 tokens per installed skill, the documented figure.
agentsExplained.skEagerNote: Every body and bundled file, on every call
agentsExplained.skActive: Bodies and files of triggered skills
agentsExplained.skillsNote: Script code never enters context: only its output does, so it is not counted here.
agentsExplained.hooksTitle: Advisory or enforced: who stops each action
agentsExplained.hooksIntro: Turn controls on and off and see which proposed actions are stopped, which ask a person and which rely only on the model following an instruction.
agentsExplained.out_advisoryOnly: Only an instruction stands in the way
agentsExplained.hooksNote: An instruction may well be followed; the point is that nothing guarantees it. Where several enforced controls cover one action, any of them blocks it.
agentsExplained.triTitle: Check an agent for the lethal trifecta
agentsExplained.triIntro: Give a support agent its tools and see which legs of the trifecta are present.
agentsExplained.triGate: A person approves every outbound message or request
agentsExplained.triAllText: Text in an inbound email or web page could instruct the agent to send private data out. Split the agent or remove a capability.
agentsExplained.triGated: All three legs, with outbound actions approved by a person.
agentsExplained.triGatedText: This depends on the reviewer noticing private data in what they approve. Removing a leg is the stronger control.
agentsExplained.triSafeText: Missing: {legs}. Keep it that way as tools are added.
agentsExplained.triBreakers: Removing any one of these breaks the trifecta: {list}.
agentsExplained.triNote: Fetching a web page counts as external communication because the request itself, including its address, reaches a server outside the organisation.

api.termsSummary: {provider} offers this model only through its API. Use is governed by the provider's commercial terms and usage policy, linked here; the weights are not released.
api.noWeights: Weights, architecture and training details are not published, so the model cannot be self-hosted, inspected or compared layer by layer.
api.cardIntro: A closed model: {provider} does not publish its architecture, parameter count or weights, so this card covers access and cost only. Architecture pages, the model diagram and Compare are available for open-weight models.

diagram.title: How {name} is built
diagram.intro: Click any box, or a layer in the strip, to see what it does in this model, with the numbers from its published configuration.
diagram.note: A simplified processing path from the model's configuration at the pinned revision and the architecture gallery. Real implementations add details such as biases and kernel-level optimisations.
diagram.repeatLayers: {name} runs the same block {n} times in sequence. Each layer reads the residual stream, refines it and passes it on.
diagram.repeatMix: Layer types in the published mix: {mix}.
diagram.repeatUnknown: The number of layers is not stated in the published configuration.
diagram.notStated: Not stated in the model's published configuration.
diagram.input: {name} receives text as characters; nothing numeric happens until the tokenizer splits it into tokens.
diagram.tokenizer: The tokenizer splits text into pieces from a fixed vocabulary of {v} entries, so every piece becomes a whole number from 0 to {max}. A larger vocabulary means fewer tokens per sentence but a larger embedding table and output layer.
diagram.embedding: Each token number selects one row of a {v} × {d} table, turning the token into a vector of {d} numbers. The table holds {p} parameters.
diagram.embeddingShare: That is {share} of the model's {total} parameters.
diagram.embeddingWidth: Each token becomes a vector of {d} numbers, and that width is carried through every layer.
diagram.normRms: RMSNorm divides each token's vector by its root mean square and applies a learned scale, keeping values in a steady range as they pass through many layers.
diagram.normLayer: LayerNorm subtracts each token's mean, divides by its standard deviation and applies a learned scale and shift, keeping values in a steady range.
diagram.normUnknown: The published configuration does not name the normalisation.
diagram.normCount: {norm} runs before the attention step and before the feed-forward step in each of the {layers} layers, plus once at the end: {n} times per token.
diagram.normFinal: A last {norm} steadies each vector after the final layer, before it is turned into scores over the vocabulary.
diagram.mixerHybrid: Not every layer uses attention. Published description: {mix}.
diagram.mixerGqa: {h} query heads, each {hd} numbers wide, look back over earlier tokens. Every {g} query heads share one of {kv} key/value heads (grouped-query attention), so each layer stores {per} numbers per token in its cache instead of {full}: {x} times less.
diagram.mixerMqa: {h} query heads, each {hd} numbers wide, share a single key/value head (multi-query attention), so each layer stores {per} numbers per token in its cache instead of {full}: {x} times less.
diagram.mixerMha: {h} heads, each {hd} numbers wide, each keep their own keys and values (multi-head attention), so each layer stores {per} numbers per token in its cache.
diagram.mixerMla: {h} query heads read keys and values compressed into a shared latent vector of {r} numbers per token (multi-head latent attention); the cache stores the latent rather than full keys and values.
diagram.mixerMlaNoRank: {h} query heads read keys and values compressed into a shared latent vector (multi-head latent attention); the configuration does not state the latent size.
diagram.mixerQk: Queries and keys are normalised before they are compared (QK-Norm), which keeps attention scores from growing too large during training.
diagram.mixerSharedKv: Some layers reuse keys and values computed by another layer, which shrinks the cache further.
diagram.mixerGlobalHead: Local layers use heads {local} numbers wide; global layers use heads {global} wide.
diagram.mixerCache: Across all its layers, {name} keeps about {kib} KiB of cache per token at 16-bit precision.
diagram.positionBase: Rotary position encoding (RoPE) rotates pairs of query and key values by angles that depend on position, with base {theta}. A larger base rotates more slowly, which suits longer contexts.
diagram.positionPartial: Only {pct}% of each head's dimensions are rotated; the rest carry no position signal.
diagram.positionScaled: {type} scaling stretches the rotations by a factor of {factor} to reach longer contexts than training used.
diagram.positionScaledFrom: {type} scaling stretches the rotations {factor} times, from the {original} tokens used in training to about {extended}.
diagram.positionLocal: Sliding-window layers use a separate base of {theta}.
diagram.positionContext: The published context length is {context} tokens.
diagram.positionNope: The attention layers use no position encoding (NoPE); token order is still implied by the causal mask and by any non-attention layers.
diagram.windowSplit: {w} of the {total} layers look back only over the last {size} tokens (sliding window); the other {f} layers see the whole context.
diagram.windowSaving: At {tokens} tokens of context, that keeps the cache at {real} GiB per session instead of {naive} GiB if every layer kept every token.
diagram.windowNone: Every attention layer sees the whole context; no sliding window is configured.
diagram.residual: Each block's output is added back to its input, the residual stream of {d} numbers per token, so each of the {n} layers adjusts the representation instead of replacing it. This is what keeps deep stacks trainable.
diagram.moe: The feed-forward block is a mixture of {e} experts, each {w} numbers wide. A router picks {k} experts for each token, and only those run.
diagram.moeShared: Shared experts: {s}, which run for every token alongside the routed ones.
diagram.moeActive: About {active} of the {total} parameters work on each token ({pct}), yet every expert must be held in memory.
diagram.moeDense: Layers with an ordinary dense feed-forward block instead of experts: {n}.
diagram.ffnDense: Each token passes on its own through a feed-forward network that widens from {d} to {w} numbers ({x} times) and back. These blocks hold most of a dense model's parameters.
diagram.outputTied: The output layer reuses the embedding table (tied weights): one {v} × {d} matrix serves both ends, saving {p} parameters.
diagram.outputUntied: A separate {d} × {v} output matrix of {p} parameters scores every vocabulary entry as the next token.
diagram.outputTiedShort: The output layer reuses the embedding table (tied weights).
diagram.outputUntiedShort: The output layer has its own weights, separate from the embedding table.
diagram.outputSoftcap: Scores are soft-capped at {cap} with a tanh, so no single score can dominate.
diagram.predict: The {v} scores become probabilities with a softmax. One token is chosen, appended to the text, and the whole pass runs again for the next token.
diagram.predictShort: The scores become probabilities with a softmax. One token is chosen, appended to the text, and the whole pass runs again for the next token.
diagram.predictMtp: Multi-token prediction modules: {n}. They also guess tokens further ahead; they are used in training and can speed up generation through speculative decoding.

cost.title: Cost planning
cost.intro: What each model costs to run for your workload: list prices for closed models through their APIs, and GPU capacity for open-weight models you host yourself. Every assumption is an input.
cost.peakHint: Busiest hour over the average hour; sizes self-hosted capacity
cost.cacheable: Input that is a repeated prefix
cost.residency: Keep inference in-region (data-residency pricing where the provider charges for it)
cost.modelsNote: Closed models are priced from the providers' list prices. Open-weight models are priced as GPU capacity on the cloud you choose; only models with a published cache size can be sized.
cost.hostIntro: How open-weight models are served. Throughput is estimated from each GPU's published memory bandwidth and compute, not measured; benchmark before you commit.
cost.hostNote: Bandwidth and compute achieved are assumptions: serving software rarely reaches the datasheet figure. 730 hours is always on.
cost.pricesFrom: Instance prices are on-demand list prices in {region}, read on {date}.
cost.customRates: Enter rates for {n} instances without a stored price
cost.monthlySub: {req} requests a month, {i} input and {o} output tokens each, at today's prices
cost.hostHow: {replicas} replicas × {nodes} node(s) of {inst} at {rate}/h · batch {batch} · about {tps} output tokens/s and {rps} requests/s per replica
cost.noInstance: No instance on this cloud fits the model with a stored or entered price.
cost.flag_noPrice: No stored price: enter a rate
cost.flag_noBandwidth: GPU bandwidth not published: no throughput estimate
cost.flag_noCompute: GPU compute not published: prefill time not counted
cost.flag_multiNode: Needs several instances per replica; assumes ideal scaling across them
cost.flag_noArch: Weights or cache size not published: cannot be sized
cost.flag_contextShort: Request longer than the model's context
cost.tableNote: API costs include cache writes, cache reads, batch share and long-context tiers as each provider publishes them. Self-hosted costs are compute only: storage, networking, engineering and support are not included.
cost.methodTitle: How the numbers are worked out
cost.formulaApi: cost = requests × (fresh input × input price + cache writes × write price + cache reads × cached price + output × output price) ÷ 1,000,000, blended with batch prices for the batch share
cost.methodApiNote: Long-context prices apply to the whole request when its input passes the provider's threshold. Prices change on the dates the providers have announced.
cost.formulaHost: replicas = ⌈peak requests/s ÷ (capacity × utilisation)⌉; capacity = 1 ÷ (prefill time + output tokens × step time ÷ batch); step time = (weights read + cache read) ÷ bandwidth achieved
cost.methodHostNote: Decoding is limited by memory bandwidth: each step reads the active weights once for the whole batch, plus every sequence's cache. Prefill is limited by compute, about 2 × active parameters operations per input token. Batch is limited by GPU memory left after the weights.
cost.noModels: Add at least one model to see costs.
cost.forecastTitle: Monthly cost over the next 12 months
cost.forecastSub: Volume grows {g}% a month; announced price changes apply from their dates
cost.forecastNote: Self-hosted capacity rises in whole replicas, so its cost moves in steps.
cost.beSub: Monthly cost against monthly volume, both on log scales; dashed lines are self-hosted
cost.beAt: {host} becomes cheaper than {api} from about {v} requests a month.
cost.beNever: {host} does not become cheaper than {api} below 1 billion requests a month.
cost.beNeedBoth: Add at least one closed and one open-weight model to see where they cross.
cost.beNote: A self-hosted replica costs the same whether it is busy or idle, so it is expensive at low volume and cheap per request at high volume. API cost rises in a straight line.

cost.gpuSpecs: GPU figures used for the throughput estimate
cost.cardWorkload: Under the cost planner's workload ({name}): {req} requests a month, {i} input and {o} output tokens each.
cost.cardHostNote: An estimate from published GPU figures and the planner's assumptions; compute only. Change the cloud, precision or workload in the cost planner.
